content: Tom Hyde, also known as Thomas E. Hyde, BA, DC, DABCO, FICC, was born in 1945 to Ida and Earle Hyde in Thomasville, Georgia. He earned his Doctor of Chiropractic degree from Logan College of Chiropractic in 1977 and his Bachelor of Arts degree in Biology from Florida State University in 1973. Following his education, he practiced chiropractic medicine in Miami, Florida, from 1977 to 1997. He is married to Susan Hyde and has one daughter, Jennifer. Dr. Hyde is recognized for his significant contributions to sports chiropractic. He served as the Secretary-General of the International Federation of Sports Chiropractic (FICS) and was the team doctor for the United States Olympic Committee during the Pan American Games held in Indianapolis, Indiana, in 1987. Additionally, he has achieved personal milestones such as summiting Mount Kilimanjaro and Mount Aconcagua, alongside numerous other professional awards and accomplishments throughout his extensive career. In his professional career, Dr. Hyde held the position of President and Executive Director of the American Chiropractic Association (ACA) Sports Council for eight years. He also served as the liaison between FICS and the World Olympians Association. In 1987, he became the first Doctor of Chiropractic to be selected to work at the United States Olympic Training Center in Colorado Springs, Colorado, as part of the volunteer chiropractor program. That same year, he was chosen to represent the United States as the team doctor at the Pan American Games in Indianapolis. In 1990, Dr. Hyde was appointed as the State of Florida's coordinator for medical services for the Sunshine Games. From 1990 to 1997, he served as the chiropractic consultant for the Miami Dolphins. In 1997, he was appointed to a four-year term on the Pan American Games and Olympic Task Force for the State of Florida. He also served on the Governor's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports. In 2001, Dr. Hyde was inducted into the ACA Sports Council Hall of Fame. In 2004, he was a member of the commission known as The Mercy Guidelines, which developed the foundational national professional guidelines for chiropractic practice. In 2006, he joined the Board of Directors of the Miami-Dade Sports Commission. In 2009, he was named Person of the Year by Dynamic Chiropractic. Dr. Hyde has lectured extensively across the globe, sharing his expertise in chiropractic medicine in countries such as the United States, Canada, Hong Kong, Japan, Mexico, Argentina, Denmark, England, France, Switzerland, Australia, Chile, Brazil, Wales, and South Africa.
